concept.name: Collateral factor
concept.definition: The collateral factor is the per-asset parameter that determines how much borrowing power a unit of deposited collateral confers, expressed as a percentage of the collateral's value; in Aave V3 this concept is split into LTV (borrowing power for new loans) and liquidation threshold (the undercollateralization trigger).
concept.intuition: It is the haircut the protocol applies to your collateral: $100 of a blue-chip asset might count as $80 of borrowing power, while a volatile token counts as far less.
concept.mechanics: Each listed asset has a governance-set collateral factor/LTV reflecting its volatility and liquidity risk. A user's total borrowing capacity is the sum over collateral assets of value × factor; borrowing beyond it is impossible, and positions drifting past the (higher) liquidation threshold become liquidatable. Riskier or less liquid assets get lower factors.
concept.formula: Borrowing capacity = Σ (collateral_i × price_i × factor_i); e.g. $10,000 ETH at 80% → $8,000 max borrow.
concept.failure_modes: Factors set too high for illiquid collateral let bad debt accumulate because liquidators cannot exit seized collateral profitably; factors changed by governance can shift risk parameters on live positions.
concept.misconceptions: The collateral factor is not the interest rate — it caps loan size, not cost. Depositing more collateral value does not always raise borrowing power proportionally if the asset has a low or zero factor.
concept.example: Aave V3's stablecoin E-Mode category uses 97% LTV and 98% liquidation threshold, while a volatile long-tail asset in isolation mode might carry 50% LTV with a hard debt ceiling.

citations.source: Frangella & Herskind, Aave V3 Technical Paper (2022)
citations.section: Section 3-4: risk parameters (LTV, liquidation threshold, liquidation bonus)
